task.title: Checking the brake fluid level
task.shortdesc: Check the brake fluid level in the reservoir periodically. The fluid level should be between the MAX and MIN marks on the side of the reservoir.

step.cmd: To prevent brake fluid contamination, clean the area around the reservoir cap thoroughly before removing the cap and adding brake fluid.

Periodically check that the fluid level in the brake fluid reservoir is between MIN and MAX. The level falls as you accumulate mileage. This is a normal condition associated with wear on the brake linings.

info.p: If the fluid level is excessively low, have the system inspected by a professional workshop. Kia recommends visiting an authorized Kia dealer or service partner.

postreq.p: Only use hydraulic brake fluid that conforms to DOT 4 specifications. (Refer to .)
Never mix different types of fluid.

note.p: If the brake system requires you to add fluid frequently, have the system inspected by a professional workshop. Kia recommends visiting an authorized Kia dealer or service partner.

When changing and adding brake fluid, handle it carefully. Do not let it come into contact with your eyes. If brake fluid comes into contact with your eyes, immediately flush them with a large quantity of fresh tap water. Have your eyes examined by a doctor as soon as possible.

Do not allow brake fluid to come into contact with the vehicle’s body paint, as it will damage the paint. Never use brake fluid that has been exposed to open air for an extended period of time, as its quality cannot be guaranteed. Properly dispose of it instead. Do not put the wrong kind of fluid into the brake fluid reservoir. A few drops of mineral-based oil (such as engine oil) in your brake system can damage the brake system parts.
